elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 7.2A: "The Issuer, as the customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement, and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement, for convenience and without cause". This is an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right; there are no Order Forms in this securitization structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. (The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present = false" is a lexical miss: the customer-side party is named "Issuer", expressly identified in the inserted text as "the customer under this Agreement".)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2A: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly 30 days, written, given by Customer to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2A: "the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely period-based) and is owed by the Vendor (Servicer).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1 No Resignation: "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." Vendor exit is limited to legal inability, so there is no Vendor convenience right at any point in the term; the drafter correctly left this favourable language untouched.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2A gives 30 days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (it is better for us, but it does not satisfy this fallback element as written).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, make-whole or instalment mechanic attaches to the new Section 7.2A right (Servicing Fees are payable in arrears), so nothing exceeds a three-month cap. The Section 8.1/8.2 Make-Whole Payment is tied to the Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption, not to Customer convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 7.1 bars Servicer resignation altogether except on legal inability, so the Vendor has no convenience right that could be exercised mid-term or at term end.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no Vendor convenience termination right under Section 7.1 to which a notice period could attach.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: Section 7.2A supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice and the pro rata prepaid-fee refund, and retained Section 7.1 already denies the Servicer any resignation/convenience right during the term.

The fallback is not met only because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90; that is immaterial since the preferred level is complete, and staying at preferred correctly avoids gifting the Servicer an end-of-term convenience right it does not have.

Minimality is satisfied: the change is a single concise insertion with no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, and it correctly omits the model language's "in whole or in part" (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists here). The appositive "as the customer under this Agreement" and "without cause" are descriptive only and impose no new obligation.

Intent fails on a contradictory retained sentence: Section 8.3 provides that "This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full ... and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement" — an exhaustive statement of when the Agreement ends. Section 7.2A purports to terminate "this Agreement" on 30 days' notice, which directly conflicts. Repair in operative language: either add to Section 8.3 the words "unless earlier terminated in accordance with Section 7.2A", or narrow Section 7.2A to terminate only "the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement" (which is all the checklist requires and matches the Section 7.2(c) removal construct).

Second intent defect to repair: Section 7.2(c) provides that Cellco reassumes the Receivables-acquisition obligations "immediately upon the removal of Cellco as Servicer pursuant to this Section 7.2", and the Successor Servicer machinery in Section 7.4 is triggered by resignation/removal under Sections 7.1 and 7.2. A termination under a new, separately numbered Section 7.2A is not a removal "pursuant to this Section 7.2" and may fall outside those triggers. Fix by drafting the new right as Section 7.2(e) (or expressly deeming termination under it a removal under Section 7.2 for purposes of Sections 7.2(c), 7.3 and 7.4) so the Successor Servicer and Cellco reassumption mechanics engage.
